region: Cool temperate and boreal forests of Europe, Asia and North America
description: Larch is one of the hardest and most durable softwoods, used for cladding, fencing, decking, boat planking, stairs and flooring. European larch, Siberian larch, western larch and tamarack are the main species in trade.

hazards.summary: The UK HSE lists nettle rash and dermatitis from larch, and notes the cause may be lichens growing on the bark rather than the wood itself.

A German carpenter with confirmed softwood allergy had IgE antibodies to larch as well as spruce and pine, but spruce was the main trigger. A larch-specific respiratory allergy has not been confirmed.
All wood dust is classified as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to this wood like every other species.

related_species_note: Cross-sensitization with spruce and pine was seen in the one documented softwood allergy case.

Warm reddish-brown to orange-brown heartwood with a narrow strip of pale yellowish sapwood along one edge. Strongly marked growth rings with sharp contrast between pale earlywood and dense dark latewood, a few small dark knots, medium-coarse texture, a slightly resinous sheen, and no visible pores. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.

notes_internal: Genus entry; image uses Larix decidua. Kespohl-2012 is a single polysensitized patient; larch sIgE present but challenge tests were with softwoods generally and spruce was dominant, so level 3 for larch (not 1). Hanslian-1964 ('Allergic diseases caused by larch wood', Czech, Prac Lek, PMID 14251055) has no abstract; route and testing unknown, so not cited. See data/verify/softwoods.md.
